why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its line, and the builder steps too. Nothing is stricter than its line. Check 1 asks for `<file>:<line>: ` followed by "a non-empty error text", not exact error wording. Check 2 only asks for non-empty stderr and exit 2. Check 4 allows "extra args only if it still runs node --test". Check 6 only asks for one PR, the Closes text and green checks. No brief sets a branch-name rule, a mutation test or a limit on which files the PR may touch. CRLF handling and the executable bit are under Advisory as "notes, not failures". Every behaviour line is checked by running something: the CLI on printf fixtures (Checks 1–2), importing `lint` (Check 3), `npm test -w jsonl-lint` (Check 4), and `npm ci && npm test` plus `gh pr checks` (Check 6). Reading files is only used for structure lines (package.json fields, test case coverage, READMEs), and Check 4 runs the tests as well.
